items.text: With this new approach to the navigation system, bigger rooms will cause humans to spend more turns inside them, making room size a much more important strategic choice. It should also address one of the last major pain points we’ve seen from the community around mansion layout and room-building.
Let's dive into some of the bigger new features... you can find the complete changes and bugfix list below.
Bigger rooms mean extra human turns

Before the update it didn't matter how large a room was, a human was always going to traverse it in one turn by default. Now however, every 8 tiles a room has a human will spend an extra turn inside of it.
For instance: a human will spend 1 turn in a 6 tile room, 2 turns in a 10 tile room and 3 turns in a 17 tile room.
To balance this out, every 8 tiles a room has, will increase the cost of tiles you want to add to said rooms.
(This also counters the big Essence overflow a lot of players have in the late-game/run)
Smaller rooms mean different mechanics
While big rooms will now give you an obvious advantage, smaller rooms will give you a disadvantage.
Rooms now have a maximum capacity of one Human per tile in the room. If this capacity is exceeded at start turn, all Humans exceeding the capacity will move to the next room.
For instance: if you have 5 humans in a group and their next room only has 4 tiles, 1 human will immediately cross the room to the next one.
Single tile rooms will always be crossed by humans in the same turn.
Rooms with <4 tiles are no longer valid targets for room targeting cards... this is also an important one!
Totems/modifiers for people that find the new small-room-debuffs a bit overwhelming
Floodgates (disable spill mechanic).
Claustrophobia (disable single tile room skip).
The new systems have been tested, but not in the thousands of players strong community, so any thoughts are welcome on the Steam Discussions and Discord https://discord.gg/MhcDeypzne!
Changes
The Exploring intent (green walking icon) has been split into:
Exploring Room: The Human will stay in the room this turn and wander around.
Using Door: The explorer will move to the next room using the highlighted door.
Humans will enter the Exploring Room state for one turn per 8 tiles in the room. In rooms with < 8 tiles they will go straight to the Using Door state.
Spill mechanic: Rooms have a maximum capacity of one Human per tile in the room. If this capacity is exceeded at start turn, all Humans exceeding the capacity will move to the next room.
Skip single tile room: Humans will skip the next room if it only has one tile. They will not trigger traps.
The cost of building tiles will increase per 8 tiles already in the room:
1-8 tiles: 5 essence per tile
8-16 tiles: 50 essence per tile
16-24 tiles: 100 essence per tile (keeps increasing by 50 per 8 tiles)

items.text: The 7th of May 2025 is when the haunted domain first opened its gates to let in hapless humans and feed off of them. Since then, the game has grown immensely and we still have some things to come like the changes you can read about below.

Thank you for haunting with us, for your feedback, reviews, workshop scenarios, videos, articles, shout outs, thumbs up and everything else. We read and watch practically all of them, and you have helped shape the game since release day. We hope this shows in all of the updates since then, including this one!
The biggest change is the human navigation/pathfinding.
When a room only has explored neighboring rooms, humans no longer take the room closest to the heart by default.
They now have a random chance to take any of the other neighbors they have not visited before.
This will avoid the “always beelining for the heart” behavior some players have reported.
Also, humans now have a higher chance to split up from a bigger group.
Another ask from a lot of players has been to nerf Pathfinders in the Easy mode, and so we have.
They are now reduced to a bare minimum.

items.text: We've got something special lined up for Deck of Haunts' one year anniversary:
A free update containing a brand new mission system that brings more meta progression into the game and contains a boatload of content including a long awaited backstory!
The mission system is something we think will greatly add to the meta-progression feel, while also giving players specific targets to achieve apart from surviving/growing.
Rewards for missions will not be linked to your current XP-level, so any unlocks you get through missions, you'll be able to immediately play with.

Curated missions: These will be very specific missions that are paired with permanent unlocks. For instance, the mission could be "Kill a Master Stonemason in the Heart room.", and the reward for that would be a positive gameplay totem “Witness”, which reduces Health and Sanity of any human witnessing your Heart to 1. Unlocks for the curated missions could be cards, rooms, story, totems and more.

Generic missions: These will be less specific and will activate when you've completed all the curated missions (and will deactivate again if there would be an update of the game containing more curated missions.). They are paired with in-run rewards. For instance, the mission could be "Raise Tension to max for 5 humans in 1 night.", and the reward for that would be "Next night all humans spawning skip their first turn.".
Missions that are not completed will carry to new nights/runs.
There currently is a batch of 22 curated missions, with more to come later this month!
Going through reviews and feedback, this seemed like an area that a lot of players found they needed more, so now, there is more!
Story unlocks will be linked to the Curated mission system, for instance the first time you drive a human insane in the same room as the Witch, you'll get her backstory as a reward.

notes.title: As this is the games' anniversary, we've also compiled some thoughts from the team at Mantis Games about the one year that has passed since release

items.text: What are your thoughts and feelings about Deck of Haunts as a project to work on and as a game, one year after launch?
Philippe - Producer & VFX Artist

I think not only did the game grow after launch, but our team became more tightly knit as it was our first -own- project together, and I am very grateful for both! I think we can be proud of Deck of Haunts both as a game and a project, and think back on it someday in the far far future with positive nostalgia.
Tim - Senior Programmer

I am very happy to see how far Deck of Haunts has come in the year since launch. At the time of release, we felt like there were so many things we still wanted to do. By now, pretty much all these things have been added and then some. I didn’t expect we could keep adding so much content.
Willem - 3D Artist & SFX

I am proud of what we have achieved with Deck of Haunts as a team. It was our first IP with this team, and the game itself was challenging to create. We all loved the game, but also for our own specific reasons which I think made the design process much more effective. Those early meetings were a great foundation for Deck of Haunts.
San - Senior 3D Artist

I think it’s amazing to see what has been achieved in such a short timespan. A lot of design issues were solved very practically and we had a great workflow with such a small team. Everyone had their specific roles in the project but it was also nice to meet together and talk about every aspect and how we could improve it together. Also seeing our game being played by so many people and streamers on a global scale was amazing to witness.
What is something you would have done differently and something you think worked out well?
Philippe - Producer & VFX Artist

It is always easy with hindsight, but I would have definitely released in Early Access first, especially knowing that we have grown the game to probably become 2-3x larger/more complex than it was at 1.0 release. It would have probably cut us some slack with reviews 👀.

The combination of growing/building the house and crafting your deck/haunting the humans has worked out rather well, as players that do not like deckbuilding games did like deck of haunts, which is awesome.
Tim - Senior Programmer
The building system went through so many changes, both big and small. By now it has become a huge cluster of old and new things and it would be nicer to just remake the parts we truly need.
The card system on the other hand has proven to be very robust and flexible when it comes to adding new functionality.
Willem - 3D Artist & SFX

With hindsight a more solid foundation and system from the start for our characters and their interaction with the world would have been nice. We are not specialised in this area which meant we had to learn on the go or work with the little experience we had with it. It was something that needed a lot of adjustment and changes, but with a limited foundation this was a challenge.
“You are the evil haunted house” This idea has worked out very well. I think it is what has drawn a lot of our players to the game, it’s a fun twist that worked well with our game.
San - Senior 3D Artist
Adding statistics tracking and in-game bug reports. Right now we look at feedback and forum posts but sometimes it’s hard to know if the silent majority agrees with that.
What is your favorite review you’ve gotten from a player?
Philippe - Producer & VFX Artist

“A terrific turn based haunted house game. Best in class.” - Coming from a player that had 410 hours of playtime when they wrote the review a month ago, and has a whopping 545.9 hours in total now 👀💖.
Tim - Senior Programmer
Seeing any review from a player with more than 50 hours in the game always blows my mind.
Willem - 3D Artist & SFX
“I have never been a house before, but I think I like it.” Seeing players enjoy the twist that Deck of Haunts brings is always a pleasure.
San - Senior 3D Artist
I love the extreme short ones “good”, “+1”, like a waiter asking if you’re enjoying your meal but your mouth is still full.
What is something you would like to tell all past, current and future players?
Philippe - Producer & VFX Artist

You’ve been amazing for all of your Steam Discussion and Discord posts, where you have actively thought about Deck of Haunts’ design and actually helped to shape the direction of the game since launch, it has been very motivating to read!
And of course, reading all those positive reviews, especially from players that spent tens or even hundreds of hours in the game, was a salve for the soul. (Well, a haunted soul.)
Tim - Senior Programmer
Thank you for your feedback and bug reports. This has allowed us to make Deck of Haunts into the best version it could possibly be, not just for us, but also for the people actually playing our game.
Willem - 3D Artist & SFX
Thank you for giving Deck of Haunts a go and for forming the game with us. Your input and feedback is important and is a huge form of motivation for us as a team.
San - Senior 3D Artist
I’d like to thank everyone for their passion, playing the game, providing feedback. It’s amazing to see something you made being enjoyed by so many.

notes.title: The biggest changes since the last update

items.text: Completely reworked the editor UI to be more intuitive and user friendly.
Added the option to customize the starting layout of the house.

Added the option to choose between human types and the Male and Female variants of the humans through the portrait selector.
The starting deck now automatically gets a tag in the Steam Workshop.

items.text: One month after releasing Deck of Haunts, we're now ready to unleash the largest update yet.
It contains something a lot of you have been wanting, a higher difficulty!
Before we start off with giving you all of the info, we want to express a big thanks to our community, you give us motivation and energy to keep pumping out all of these updates.
And as always, if you like the game, a review is greatly appreciated, as it helps us a lot!
New game mode: Nightmare (Unlocked through playing a 28-day run first).
New trap cards and trap starter deck.
Crypt room and Grim Reaper (Unlocked through completing Nightmare).
New achievement.
Portraits of dead humans now disappear to make room.
New traits.
Raised the level cap from 10 to 12.
Most importantly, we added "Jason" to the pool of names for humans, it is Friday the 13th, after all.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227801/7c25ee8c787681ad6908be5195382d0c5e70e874.jpg"]
Instead of just scaling some numbers to make the game more difficult, we've made an entirely new game mode: Nightmare.
In Nightmare, you will have to survive 13 Nightmares consisting of 13 nights each.
During those nights you will encounter increasingly difficult curated groups of humans, some of them even containing new traits.
To make matters even more dangerous, every Nightmare will have a specific new modifier applied to it, which will carry over to the next Nightmare.
A new mechanic & professional scythe wielder has also been introduced in Nightmare: the Grim Reaper.
Whenever you kill or drive a human insane, you will collect a soul.
Once you've filled up your meter to 13, you can exchange those souls for a visit from the Grim Reaper, who will Harvest a human in your house of your choosing.

If you can survive the final Nightmare, 13, you will have won over the confidence in your haunting skills of the Grim Reaper, and you will be able to permanently add them to your house in other game modes with the Crypt room that you'll unlock.
These are the extra unlocks you can achieve in the Nightmare mode:
Card: Corpse Explosion.
Room: Crypt.
Card: Sleep Paralysis.
Achievement.
Upon reaching XP-level 12, you will unlock the new Trap deck.
To make trap decks more viable, we've added 5 new trap cards:
Leaking Rust
Improvised Snare
Collective Toll
Amplify Agony
Dragged Under
For some quality of life and more polish, we've added some other things to the game, such as:
Death animation of the heart, when you lose a night.
Removal of portraits of dead humans.
Setting a counter of turns on humans with the "Helpline" trait.

We're very proud to push this update live, as we know it is something that a lot of you have been wanting since release day... Starter decks and a more varied run-system!
Always wanted to try a Sanity or Damage driven deck? Time to try that out.
Or, if you are a player that loves to give themselves over to the "luck of the draw", there is also a chaos starter deck now that will select cards from your unlocked collection.
Apart from the starter decks (more of them to come as well in the future!), we've also spent some time on revamping the runs themselves.

Added to the now "Classic" very first run, where you previously could only re-run pretty much the same thing (albeit with some minor variation in stats/human amount/traits), we now have a run-system that will, every night, pick from a selection of more curated nights.

So, where in one run you might have a night where you get a solid group of high health regenerative humans with doctor bags that spawn in just 1 wave, in the next run that very same night might instead have you encounter 6 waves of fragile, steadfast humans with a compass.
The beauty of this system is, that we can keep on adding different curated runs into the mix to make sure you get an increased amount of variations in your runs!
As a sneak peek: we're currently creating a set of new cards to add to the game, together with a new starter deck type.
